clue.text: Mr Cruise takes a cruise, first on one river then another

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A film star enjoys a river cruise that moves from one waterway to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on one river' puts PO in front of the rest; 'another' is the definition, a second river: POTOMAC, which flows through Washington DC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is a North American waterway, so it is a different river from the Italian Po used in the wordplay.

clue.text: Father waits outside for fruit

indicators.note: outside asks for just the two letters at the edges of the word

blocks.note: a child's word for a father

explanation.surface: A dad hangs about outdoors before going off for some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waits outside' looks like a father standing outdoors, but it means the outside letters of waits.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaws, also spelt pawpaws, are tropical fruits, another name for papayas, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Short treatises about street transport

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the joined words run from the far end

blocks.note: a cart is a simple means of transport

explanation.surface: Brief essays dealing with roads and public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: ST and CART together read backwards give TRACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet or essay arguing a religious or political point, so brief treatises in the plural.

clue.text: Psychic worker going underground without fear

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: a miner works below the surface

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant labourer goes down the pit with no sense of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without fear' reads as fearless, but without is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind-reader claims to know others' thoughts by telepathy, which is exactly what a psychic noun describes.

clue.text: Animal taking cover on island

blocks.note: a coat covers, as a coat of paint

explanation.surface: A creature seeks shelter on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a raccoon-like mammal with a long snout from the Americas, so a specific animal.

clue.text: Some milk I left for a duck

blocks.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk, from an old advertising slogan

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a little milk out to feed a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: PINTA, a pint of milk, comes from the 1950s British slogan 'Drinka Pinta Milka Day'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pintail is a slender dabbling duck with a long pointed tail, so it names one kind of waterfowl.

clue.text: Dolly bird entered temple

indicators.note: something that has entered is now inside the other word

explanation.surface: A girl went into a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly bird is British slang for an attractive young woman, but here Dolly is the singer and bird a hen: PART(HEN)ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the ancient Greek shrine to Athena on the Acropolis of Athens.

clue.text: Regency architect from the north remains

blocks.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A Regency architect's body is brought back from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash designed Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion during the British Regency era of the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: A game soldier taking arrowhead for self-defence

blocks.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the head of arrow is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A brave soldier takes up an arrow to protect himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrowhead' is a single word in the surface, split as the head of arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written justification of one's own beliefs or conduct, a defence of oneself.

clue.text: Spartan commander given only half a tool

indicators.note: only half means one of the two halves of that word is thrown away

blocks.note: a sander is a power tool for smoothing wood

explanation.surface: A frugal general receives just half a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan' suggests austere, but it means from Sparta; the back half of only, LY, is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysander was the admiral of ancient Sparta who defeated the Athenian fleet and ended the Peloponnesian War.

clue.text: It's not fair to mourn

definitions.note: an infinitive phrase for the verb

blocks.note: first meaning: not pretty, homely in looks
second meaning: an old verb for lament, as in complain

explanation.surface: A grieving person protests that life is unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fair' sounds like a complaint about injustice, but fair here means good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means unattractive in appearance, the opposite of fair, and as an archaic verb it means to lament or grieve.

clue.text: Wearing a metal jacket, one gets no back injuries

indicators.note: back means the word no is read from its end
wearing a jacket means being wrapped inside it

blocks.note: brass is a metal alloy, here the outer layer

explanation.surface: A soldier in a metal-jacketed vest comes through without any back injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal jacket' sounds like body armour; it means the metal forms an outer layer round one and the turned word no.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasions are scrapes where skin has been rubbed away, a common kind of minor wound.

clue.text: Drunk after drink is unassailable

indicators.note: after places the first-named word behind the second one

explanation.surface: Someone drunk after drinking feels invincible.
explanation.definitionFit: A watertight argument or case has no flaws through which it could be attacked, so it is beyond challenge.

clue.text: Petty Officer with navy blue material

explanation.surface: A naval officer brings a navy-blue fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'navy blue' reads as a colour, but navy is RN and blue means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in British usage means indecent or obscene, so blue material is pornographic content.

clue.text: Mythical murderer misleading court and press

indicators.note: misleading suggests the letters are led astray into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of court and press

explanation.surface: A legendary killer deceives the judiciary and the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Procrustes was the Greek legend's bandit who stretched or lopped his guests to fit his bed, killing them.

clue.text: A recruit on a manoeuvre? Not at all!

indicators.note: a manoeuvre moves troops about, so these letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of a recruit on a

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a raw recruit is on exercise and gets a flat denial.
explanation.definitionFit: Au contraire is a French phrase used in English meaning on the contrary, a firm denial of what was said.

clue.text: Ragged cheer once needed sticking together

indicators.note: something ragged is torn and messy, so the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: A rowdy cheer once called for some team unity.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherence is the quality of parts holding together, literally cohesion and figuratively logical consistency.

clue.text: Damned prosecutor finally smothered by one on trial

indicators.note: finally asks for only the closing letter of that word
smothered means covered over entirely, so it ends up inside the other word

blocks.note: the accused is the person being tried

explanation.surface: A cursed lawyer is overwhelmed by the defendant in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damned prosecutor' reads as one phrase, but Damned stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means under a curse, doomed or condemned, the same sense as damned.

clue.text: Chess expert losing last three family members

indicators.note: losing last three says the final trio of letters is dropped

blocks.note: a grandmaster is a top-ranked chess player

explanation.surface: A chess champion drops three games at the end of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandmothers, informally grandmas, are relatives two generations up, so they belong to a family.

clue.text: Noted Spanish gypsy taking tea break - one caught by service provider

indicators.note: taking means holding something within, so the gypsy is split open around it

blocks.note: Carmen is the gypsy heroine of Bizet's opera, so noted as in set to music
cha is British slang for tea
c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A famous Spanish gypsy pauses for tea, then is snared by someone offering a service.
explanation.walkthrough: Noted hints at music: Carmen is Bizet's opera heroine. Cha is British slang for tea, and c for caught comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A car mechanic services vehicles, and a car service is the routine maintenance a garage provides.

clue.text: Part of a wooden seat from Hans Christian Andersen's birthplace

indicators.note: part of signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: letters running across wooden and seat

explanation.surface: A piece of a wooden bench taken from the fairy-tale writer's hometown.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is the Danish city on the island of Funen where the fairy-tale author was born in 1805.

clue.text: Prepare girl for battle with the fleet

blocks.note: to arm is to make ready for fighting
completes the phrase begun by prepare, padding inside it

explanation.surface: A girl is readied to go to war alongside the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'prepare for battle' is split by the girl's name; only its first word supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a great fleet of warships, especially the Spanish one sent against England in 1588.

clue.text: Vessels a Scottish poet topped

indicators.note: topped means having its top cut off, and in a down-reading sense the first letter goes

explanation.surface: Some vessels belonged to a Scottish poet who was executed.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are tall vases or containers, so vessels in the sense of receptacles rather than ships.

clue.text: A paid athlete has to go down deeper

blocks.note: a ship founders when it sinks

explanation.surface: A professional sportsman is forced to sink lower in the rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound means deep, physically or intellectually, so the comparative form matches deeper.

clue.text: Fair odds allowed for a piece of meat

indicators.note: odds means the letters in the odd-numbered places

blocks.note: first and third letters of Fair

explanation.surface: A bookmaker offers reasonable odds on a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair odds' sounds like betting, but means the odd letters of fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A filet is a boneless cut of beef or fish, the French spelling of fillet.

clue.text: Hairstyle for revolutionary or sportsmen

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the joined words run from the end

blocks.note: the FA, the Football Association, governs English football

explanation.surface: A haircut fit for a rebel or a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel, but it is the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy natural hairstyle associated with the 1970s.

clue.text: Match at sea in sea film

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are in disarray

blocks.note: the letters of in sea film

explanation.surface: A contest at sea appears in a seafaring movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinal is a game in a knockout competition whose winner advances to the final.

clue.text: Country where native leader is seen in Roman costume

indicators.note: a leader is the one in front, here the opening letter
seen in places it inside the garment that follows

blocks.note: the toga was the robe of a Roman citizen

explanation.surface: A tribal chief is spotted wearing a Roman robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'native leader' looks like a chief, but leader just means the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom of islands in the South Pacific, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Do spies change place in order?

indicators.note: change asks for the letters to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether secret agents swap positions in a regular sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change place' looks like one phrase; the definition starts at place.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispose, in its older sense, is to arrange or set out things in a particular arrangement.

clue.text: Piece of mosaic Greek god put back

indicators.note: back means the joined words are read from their end

blocks.note: Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A god from Greek myth is restored to his place in a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square tiles of stone or glass that make up a mosaic.
